description: Comprehensive reasoning vault for geometry formulas, perimeter, area of polygons and circles, volume of solids, angle relationships, and composite geometric modeling.

archetypes.name: Perimeter of Rectangles and Regular Polygons
archetypes.coreConcept: Perimeter is the total linear distance around the exterior boundary: P = 2L + 2W.
archetypes.mentalModel: Walking along the fence line of a rectangular enclosure.

archetypes.name: Area of Rectangles and Right Triangles
archetypes.coreConcept: Area measures two-dimensional surface coverage: rectangle area A = L * W, triangle area A = (1/2) * b * h.
archetypes.mentalModel: Tiling a plane with unit square squares versus bisecting a rectangle.
archetypes.governingRelation: A_{\text{rect}} = L \cdot W \land A_{\text{tri}} = \frac{1}{2} b h

archetypes.name: Circumference of Circles and Ratio Invariance
archetypes.coreConcept: The circumference of a circle is proportional to its diameter by constant pi: C = 2*pi*r.
archetypes.mentalModel: Unrolling the outer rim of a circular wheel along a flat path.

archetypes.name: Area of Circles via Radius Squaring
archetypes.coreConcept: The area enclosed by a circle is pi times the square of the radius: A = pi * r^2.
archetypes.mentalModel: Slicing a circle into wedge sectors rearranged into a pseudo-rectangle of width r and length pi*r.

archetypes.name: Volume of Rectangular Solids and Prisms
archetypes.coreConcept: Volume measures three-dimensional space capacity: V = L * W * H.
archetypes.mentalModel: Stacking unit cubic blocks into a three-dimensional rectangular grid.

archetypes.name: Volume of Right Circular Cylinders
archetypes.coreConcept: Volume of a cylinder is base area multiplied by height: V = pi * r^2 * h.
archetypes.mentalModel: Extruding a circular base through vertical height h.

archetypes.name: Complementary and Supplementary Angle Relationships
archetypes.coreConcept: Solve for unknown angles in complementary (90 degrees) or supplementary (180 degrees) pairs via algebraic equations or multi-step geometric constraints.
archetypes.mentalModel: Decomposing an angle pair into algebraic expressions summing to a right or straight angle.

archetypes.name: Triangle Interior Angle Sum Invariance
archetypes.coreConcept: The sum of the interior angle measures of any Euclidean triangle is identically 180 degrees.
archetypes.mentalModel: Bringing all three triangle vertices together along a straight line.

archetypes.name: Composite Facade Area with Pythagorean Gable and Cut-Out
archetypes.coreConcept: A facade is a rectangle topped by an isosceles triangular gable whose height is not given, only the rafter (slant) length. Pythagoras on half the base gives the gable height, which feeds the triangle area; the area of a circular window is then subtracted.
archetypes.mentalModel: Derived dimension (gable height) feeds a composite add-and-subtract area model.
archetypes.governingRelation: h = \sqrt{s^2 - \left(\frac{W}{2}\right)^2},\quad A = L W + \tfrac12 W h - \pi \rho^2

archetypes.name: Capacity-to-Coating Cylindrical Surface Modeling
archetypes.coreConcept: A cylindrical tank is specified by its capacity and height, not its radius. Back-solving V = pi r^2 h gives the radius, which feeds the lateral area 2 pi r h; the area then sets the number of paint cans (rounded up).
archetypes.mentalModel: Reverse-solve one formula (volume) to obtain the input of a second (lateral area).
archetypes.governingRelation: r = \sqrt{\frac{V}{\pi h}},\quad A_{\text{lat}} = 2\pi r h,\quad n = \left\lceil \frac{A_{\text{lat}}}{c} \right\rceil

archetypes.name: Area of Trapezoidal Cross-Sections
archetypes.coreConcept: The area of a trapezoid is the average of parallel bases multiplied by perpendicular height: A = (1/2)*(b1 + b2)*h.
archetypes.mentalModel: Averaging two parallel boundaries into an equivalent rectangular strip.

archetypes.name: Volume of Right Circular Cones
archetypes.coreConcept: The volume of a cone is exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with identical base and height: V = (1/3)*pi*r^2*h.
archetypes.mentalModel: Pyramidal convergence of circular slices toward an apex.

archetypes.name: Transversal Angle Pairs on Parallel Lines
archetypes.coreConcept: Consecutive interior angles formed by a transversal intersecting parallel lines sum to 180 degrees; setup and solve linear algebraic equations to determine angle measures.
archetypes.mentalModel: Sliding an intersection template along parallel rails and setting up algebraic sums.

archetypes.name: Slope-Limited Ramp Run and Length Synthesis
archetypes.coreConcept: An access ramp must not be steeper than 1:k. The slope ratio turns the required rise into a minimum horizontal run, which then feeds Pythagoras for the ramp surface length; the run is finally checked against the available space.
archetypes.mentalModel: A ratio constraint produces a leg that feeds a right-triangle hypotenuse.

archetypes.name: Budget-Limited Annular Path Width
archetypes.coreConcept: A ring-shaped path of uniform width will surround a circle of radius r. The paving budget and the price per square meter fix the largest path area; back-solving the annulus area gives the outer radius, and the path width is R - r (rounded down to the stated precision so the budget is not exceeded).
archetypes.mentalModel: Budget -> area (rate) -> outer radius (inverse annulus formula) -> width.

archetypes.name: Composite Silo Volume with Slant-Defined Cone Roof
archetypes.coreConcept: A silo is a cylinder with a conical roof; the roof is given by its slant length, not its height. Pythagoras gives the cone height, which feeds the composite volume V = V_cyl + V_cone (or, given the total capacity, back-solve the cylinder height).
archetypes.mentalModel: A derived height (from the slant) feeds the sum of two solid volumes.
archetypes.governingRelation: h_2 = \sqrt{s^2 - r^2},\quad V = \pi r^2 h_1 + \tfrac13 \pi r^2 h_2
